back: $\operatorname{softmax}(QK^\top/\sqrt{d_k})\,V$, softmax over each row (the key axis).
Query: what I look for. Key: what I advertise. Value: what I hand over if selected. Output = weighted average of values.

front: How are Q, K, V computed?
Shape of the score / weight matrix
back: $(T,T)$ per head, $(B,T,T)$ batched; row $i$ = distribution of token $i$ over all tokens.

front: Variance of $q\cdot k$ for unit-variance independent entries

back: $\operatorname{Var}(s/\sqrt{d_k})=1$. It avoids near-one-hot softmax whose Jacobian is almost zero (vanishing gradient).
$\partial p_i/\partial s_j=p_i(\delta_{ij}-p_j)$. Near 0 when $p$ is one-hot.

front: Time and memory of attention in $T$
back: $O(T^2d_k)$ time, $O(T^2)$ memory per head; constant sequential depth.

front: Why subtract the row max in softmax?
back: Softmax is shift invariant; subtracting the max prevents overflow of $e^{s}$ without changing the result.
$z_i=\sum_j a_{ij}v_j$, a convex combination of value vectors; $Z=AV$, shape $(T,d_v)$.
Self: Q, K, V from the same sequence. Cross: Q from one sequence, K and V from another.

front: Why separate key and value projections?
back: Finding a token (key) and using its content (value) are different jobs; two maps let the model learn both.
Attention links any two tokens in one step and parallelises over the sequence, at $O(T^2)$ cost; an RNN is $O(T)$ but sequential.
